summary: A 1958 light on the headland at the mouth of François Bay, Newfoundland, after a 1929 fog alarm; the 1966 tower is a federal heritage building reached only by boat.

access.note: Reached only by boat. Canadian Coast Guard property. The sources name no public access; the view they name is from the François-Grey River-Burgeo ferry.

events.note: Fog alarm station erected on West Point; alarm sounded by compressed air from an oil engine
Albert Dollimont killed at the station while unloading drums of oil (LighthouseFriends only)
Light established on West Point atop a 4.25 m square pyramidal tower
Combined light tower and fog alarm building replaced the older structures; one-storey keepers' duplex built
Historic tower inactive since 2015 per the Lighthouse Directory; active light on a skeletal tower in front

corrections.why: 1929 is the year the fog alarm was erected. LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory both give 1958 for the light. The record's events list repeats 1929 as first_lit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record dates the station from 1929, the fog alarm year. The light itself was established in 1958 (LighthouseFriends, Lighthouse Directory). Both 1929 and 1958 are kept, with the fog alarm and the light labelled separately.
The 1966 combined tower and fog building is dated the same by Parks Canada and LighthouseFriends.

notes_for_editor: Dollimont's 1950 death and Durnford's role rest on LighthouseFriends alone and are not corroborated; LighthouseFriends is copyrighted, so the story paraphrases it and quotes only short fragments. Dates 1929 (fog alarm) and 1958 (light) come from LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory; no official source for them was read (Canadian Marine annual reports in the corpus end in 1924 and Newfoundland's lights were not federal until 1949). Tower height disagrees: 4.7 m on the Coast Guard list (which may describe the active light's skeletal structure rather than the 1966 tower), about 14 m concrete in the Lighthouse Directory, a 4.25 m square pyramidal tower in 1958 per LighthouseFriends, and a two-storey wood tower per Parks Canada; the story states the disagreement. The Coast Guard list entry was read from a cached copy with no date; it still shows the light active, while the Lighthouse Directory says the historic tower has been inactive since 2015 (status and the 2015 'deactivated' event are both kept; the record's status 'active' was not changed). MarineRadar (a ship-tracking site) repeats the 1929 and 1958 dates but calls the tower concrete and 14 m, so it was not used. The MUN Maritime History Archive photo caption (Record 3799, 'Francois - entrance showing lighthouse and fog alarm') timed out and was not read. The Wikipedia article returned raw wiki markup and was not used. Chronicling America search for Francois and Newfoundland 1929 to 1960 gave no relevant page. Staffing as of any date is not sourced and is left out. Shape: five chapters for moderate evidence (the guide asks for 2 to 4); left for the editor. The Coast Guard list values were read from the cached copy: focal height 46.0 m, structure 4.7 m, range 12, Fl G 6s, green.
